newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran says money to Bosnia for relief purposes.
newsitem.headline: Iran says money to Bosnia for relief purposes.

text.p: Iran's foreign minister said in remarks broadcast on Thursday that any money Iran gave to Bosnia's main Moslem party was for relief purposes and not the election campaign of then Bosnian President Alija Izetbegovic.

Ali Akbar Velayati was responding to a question by Cable News Network television on U.S. media reports that the CIA had evidence that Iranian agents secretly delivered at least $500,000 in cash to Izetbegovic.

"I think one of the sources of the baseless allegation is the CIA. We have heard lots of baseless allegations from the CIA and some of your newspapers. Maybe one of the functions they have is making such baseless allegations," Velayati said.

"We have helped the Bosnian government and the people of Bosnia, but it was quite open and clear and we have sent them humanitarian aid.... We said the government of Bosnia should use it for humanitarian purposes and not for Mr Izetbegovic or other people in his party."

Izetbegovic's party said earlier this month it had received $500,000 in cash from Iran but the funds were used for legitimate humanitarian charities and scholarship funds for students in the country's Moslem-Croat Federation.
Izetbegovic won the most votes in a presidential race in Bosnia's peacetime elections in September and now serves as chairman of the three-member collective presidency.
